information.content: Third-generation cephalosporin reserved for serious susceptible Gram-negative infection, including Pseudomonas-suspect disease. Regular dosing is needed to keep levels above the MIC.
EMA category B Restrict. Use culture/sensitivity where possible. Avoid oral cephalosporins in small herbivores and monitor renal risk with nephrotoxic combinations.
Triazole antifungal with useful penetration into CNS, respiratory tissues and urine. Used for selected Candida, Cryptococcus, dermatophyte and other fungal infections.
Reduce dose in renal impairment and use caution in liver disease. Avoid in pregnancy/lactation and monitor hepatic tolerance.
Allylamine antifungal used for dermatophytosis and selected systemic/subcutaneous fungal disease, including avian aspergillosis and reptile fungal infections.
Monitor CBC, renal and liver values during prolonged courses. GI signs and increased liver enzymes can occur.
Tetracycline antibiotic used for susceptible infections including chlamydial and mycoplasmal disease. Long avian courses are common for chlamydiosis protocols.
Do not combine casually with bactericidal antibiotics. Handle as a potential teratogen and avoid calcium/cation interference with oral absorption.
Cestocide/trematodicide used for tapeworms and flukes in mammals and birds, and fish trematode protocols where product-specific guidance is followed.
For fish/pond use, do not combine with other pond treatments and manage filtration as directed by product instructions.
Sulphonamide anticoccidial used in ferrets, rabbits, rodents, hedgehogs, primates, birds and reptiles, including bearded dragon coccidiosis protocols.
Maintain hydration and use caution in renal compromise, especially reptiles. Sulphonamide adverse effects and crystalluria are possible.

warnings.warning_text: Reserve for confirmed susceptible serious infections; use culture/sensitivity where possible.
Avoid oral administration in small herbivores due to enterotoxaemia risk.
Reduce dose in renal impairment and use caution in liver disease.
Do not use in pregnant or lactating animals.
Prolonged courses should include CBC, renal and liver monitoring where feasible.
Do not combine with bactericidal antimicrobials unless specifically justified.
Potential teratogen; avoid handling exposure in pregnant people.
Do not use at the same time as other fish or pond treatments; manage UV/carbon filters according to product instructions.
Some products are restricted to specific pond species and should not be used in ponds containing orfe or terrapins.
Sulphonamide crystals can form in concentrated or acidic urine; maintain hydration and avoid urinary acidifiers.
Use with care in reptiles with reduced renal function, renal failure or dehydration.
Sulphonamide hypersensitivity reactions including severe dermatological reactions are possible.

contraindications.notes: Avoid unless no alternative and specialist rationale.

contraindications.contraindication: No firm species-specific contraindication, but avoid casual use without fungal diagnosis.
Concurrent bactericidal antimicrobial therapy unless specifically indicated.
Keratoconjunctivitis sicca or prior sulphonamide adverse reaction.
Renal disease, renal failure or dehydration unless benefit clearly outweighs risk.

adverse_effects.effect: Injection pain, GI disturbance and enterotoxaemia risk in small herbivores if used orally.
Nausea, diarrhoea, vomiting in birds and possible hepatotoxicity.
Vomiting, diarrhoea, pruritus and increased liver enzymes.
GI upset, oesophageal irritation where applicable, photosensitivity and altered gut flora.
Oral administration may cause anorexia, vomiting where possible, lethargy or diarrhoea.
Hypersensitivity, thyroid suppression, severe dermatological reactions and urinary crystal formation.

pearls.pearl: Ceftazidime is not a casual antibiotic sprinkle. Save it for serious culture-supported infections.
Fluconazole reaches useful places, but kidneys and liver still get a vote.
Fungal cases are marathons in tiny shoes. Monitor liver values before the finish line disappears.
For avian chlamydiosis, dose accuracy and course duration matter more than heroic enthusiasm.
Fish treatments are water treatments too. Filters, UV and tank-mates are part of the prescription.
With sulphonamides, hydration is the anti-crystal spell. Keep the urine river flowing.

species_warnings.warning: Avoid oral administration; use parenteral route only where justified.
Dose interval is species and temperature dependent; do not collapse all reptiles into one plan.
Vomiting has been reported; monitor appetite and hydration.
High-dose reports exist, but lower clinical ranges may be effective for dermatophytosis; monitor tolerance.
Macaws may need lower long-acting injectable dose rates; long chlamydiosis courses require strict protocol compliance.
Do not combine with other treatments and follow filtration restrictions for the exact product.
Renal disease or dehydration makes sulphonamide use riskier.
Water medication protocols depend on intake; sick birds may underdose themselves.

interactions.mechanism: Do not mix in the same syringe; clinical synergy can exist if administered separately.
interactions.recommendation: Administer separately and monitor renal status.

interactions.mechanism: Loop diuretics can increase nephrotoxicity risk with cephalosporins.
Bacteriostatic drugs may reduce beta-lactam bactericidal activity.

interactions.recommendation: Monitor for tachycardia, tremor or seizures.

interactions.mechanism: Fluconazole can increase ciclosporin blood levels.
interactions.recommendation: Monitor and adjust ciclosporin where used.

interactions.mechanism: Potential additive hepatic burden during prolonged courses.
interactions.recommendation: Monitor liver values and avoid unnecessary combinations.

interactions.mechanism: Cations can reduce oral tetracycline absorption.
Tetracyclines may antagonise bactericidal antibiotic action.
interactions.recommendation: Avoid combination unless there is a specific rationale.

interactions.mechanism: Concurrent pond treatments may increase toxicity or treatment failure risk.
interactions.recommendation: Do not combine unless product guidance allows.

interactions.mechanism: Acidic urine increases sulphonamide crystal formation risk.
interactions.recommendation: Avoid urinary acidifiers and maintain hydration.

interactions.mechanism: Procaine is a PABA precursor and may inhibit sulphonamide action.
